name: Geneva
meta_description: TDSC investigative consulting in matters touching Geneva: commodity trader diligence, wealth and asset tracing, arbitration support and integrity checks.
hero_lede: Investigative consulting for matters touching Geneva, scoped from Nashville: research on commodity trading houses and their counterparties, ownership and asset tracing around private wealth structures, and factual support for counsel in Geneva arbitration and cross-border recovery, conducted with close attention to Swiss legal limits.
intro: Geneva is a city-canton of about 639,000 residents at the end of 2024, more than 41 percent of them foreign nationals, and one of the world's main centres of diplomacy, finance and commodity trading. It hosts the United Nations' European headquarters, 38 international governmental organisations and 461 NGOs, employing around 36,000 people with permanent missions and consulates. Multinationals are central to its economy: 2,133 were present in 2019, accounting for about 37 percent of jobs and 56 percent of cantonal GDP. Geneva also generated 58.4 percent of Switzerland's commodity trading value added in 2024, according to the first federal statistics on the sector, alongside a long-established private banking and wealth management industry.

Organisations commission investigative work connected to Geneva because it is where trading decisions, wealth structures and international disputes meet. Banks, insurers and counterparties need reliable background on trading companies whose cargoes, financing and owners are spread across several continents. Creditors and estates pursue assets held through Geneva-administered companies, trusts and accounts. Politically exposed persons and their advisers often use Geneva service providers, raising integrity and sanctions questions. Arbitration seated in Geneva generates demand for factual research on parties and assets. International organisations and NGOs commission integrity due diligence on partners and suppliers, and sometimes face misconduct allegations that require careful, privilege-aware handling.

matters.title: Commodity trader counterparty diligence
matters.text: Background research on Geneva-based trading houses, brokers and their counterparties before financing, offtake or joint venture arrangements, covering ownership, management, litigation, sanctions exposure and trade reporting, so banks and partners understand who controls the cargo, the credit and the risk.

matters.title: Cargo and trade finance fraud
matters.text: Fact-finding for lenders and insurers where shipments financed through Geneva banks or traders appear duplicated, misdescribed or diverted, including research into the parties, vessels, related companies and prior disputes to support counsel in recovery, insurance claims and arbitration.

matters.title: Private wealth and asset tracing
matters.text: Mapping companies, foundations and trusts administered from Geneva, and the professionals who serve them, to help creditors, liquidators and estates identify assets and controllers, using Swiss commercial register data, foreign registries, court records and published proceedings, within the limits of Swiss banking and professional secrecy.

matters.title: PEP and sanctions-related integrity checks
matters.text: Integrity due diligence on clients, investors and counterparties connected to Geneva wealth structures where politically exposed persons, sanctioned individuals or state-linked entities may be involved, distinguishing documented facts from allegation and supporting counsel's assessment of Swiss, EU, UK and US sanctions exposure.

matters.title: International organisation partner integrity
matters.text: Integrity research on implementing partners, suppliers and grantees for Geneva-based international organisations and NGOs, and support to counsel or oversight units handling misconduct allegations, scoped around privileges, immunities and the internal rules that govern how such inquiries may proceed.

local_context.title: Geneva courts
local_context.text: Civil and commercial disputes in the canton are heard by the Tribunal de première instance, with appeals to the Cour de justice, Geneva's cantonal court of appeal. Unlike Zurich, Bern, St. Gallen and Aargau, Geneva does not have a specialised commercial court. Federal appeals go to the Federal Supreme Court in Lausanne. Court proceedings are in French, and published cantonal decisions are often anonymised, which limits their usefulness for identifying parties without counsel's involvement.

local_context.title: Arbitration in Geneva
local_context.text: Geneva is one of the world's leading arbitration seats, governed by Chapter 12 of the Swiss Private International Law Act for international cases. The Swiss Arbitration Centre administers cases under the Swiss Rules from offices including Geneva, with roots in the Geneva Chamber of Commerce, Industry and Services, and the WIPO Arbitration and Mediation Center is based in the city. Investigative support is limited to factual research for counsel and the parties.

local_context.title: Geneva commercial register
local_context.text: The cantonal commercial register is public and can be searched free of charge online, with free downloadable extracts for registered entities and paid certified extracts and statutes for companies such as SA and Sàrl. A company's physical file can also be consulted. Federal search across cantons is available through Zefix. Register entries show officers, signatory powers, capital and corporate changes, but shareholders of companies limited by shares are generally not listed.

local_context.title: Swiss legal limits on fact-finding
local_context.text: Swiss criminal law restricts gathering information for foreign authorities or parties in some circumstances, bank and professional secrecy remain significant, and the Federal Act on Data Protection applies to personal data. Private investigation and security activity in French-speaking cantons is subject to cantonal rules, so field steps in Geneva must be checked with local counsel before they are taken. These constraints shape what can be done and in what order.

local_context.title: International Geneva
local_context.text: The UN Office at Geneva and international organisations with headquarters agreements give the city a large community of staff, missions and NGOs. Twenty-four of the 38 organisations have headquarters agreements with Switzerland. Allegations involving international civil servants or diplomatic personnel raise questions of immunity and internal jurisdiction, so any inquiry is planned with the organisation's legal office or the client's counsel from the start.

tdsc_approach: For matters touching Geneva, TDSC first reviews with the client and Swiss counsel whether any information is intended for foreign courts or authorities, because Swiss law restricts some forms of fact-gathering for foreign use. Research is then carried out from Nashville using the Geneva commercial register and Zefix, the Swiss Official Gazette of Commerce, published judgments, sanctions lists, foreign registries and French-language media. Banking and professional secrecy are respected; TDSC does not seek account or client information. Where interviews, site visits or document retrieval in Geneva are justified, TDSC coordinates with appropriately authorised Swiss professionals and counsel, and personal data is handled consistently with Swiss data protection law.

faqs.q: Can you find out who owns a Geneva company?
faqs.a: The Geneva commercial register shows directors, signatories, capital and corporate history, but generally not the shareholders of an SA. We combine register data with published notices, court records, foreign registries for parent entities and media to build a picture of control. Where ownership cannot be established from lawful public sources, we say so and outline options for counsel.

faqs.q: Can you trace assets held through Geneva banks?
faqs.a: We do not obtain bank account information; Swiss banking secrecy protects it and seeking it unlawfully is a criminal matter. We identify companies, foundations, property and business interests that may hold or reflect assets, and the service providers connected to them. That research supports counsel in deciding whether to seek court orders, attachment or mutual legal assistance.

faqs.q: How do you research Geneva commodity traders?
faqs.a: We review register entries, group structures abroad, published disputes and arbitration-related court decisions, sanctions and enforcement actions, trade press and shipping information. Many traders operate through subsidiaries in Dubai, Singapore, London or offshore centres, so we follow the structure beyond Switzerland. Reporting distinguishes documented facts from market rumour, which is common in the sector.

faqs.q: Do Swiss rules on foreign proceedings affect your work?
faqs.a: They can. Swiss criminal law restricts certain acts carried out for foreign states and certain disclosures of business information abroad. If research or interviews are intended for US or other foreign litigation or regulators, we raise this with the client's Swiss counsel at the outset so the method and the channel for any evidence are agreed before work starts.

faqs.q: Does TDSC have an office in Geneva?
faqs.a: No. TDSC is based in Nashville and has no office, staff or address in Geneva or elsewhere in Switzerland. Most work is desk-based research. Where on-the-ground steps are needed, we coordinate with appropriately authorised Swiss professionals acting lawfully alongside the client's Swiss counsel, and we decline requests involving secrecy-protected information or covert methods.
